The doubling (shadda) on the nūn is not part of the base word: it results from the 'l' of 'al-' assimilating into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), so 'al-nabiyy' is pronounced 'an-nabiyy'. The base noun is نَبِيّ (nabiyy). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or the one being described.
2.root: Two derivations are held by grammarians: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, weighty information (one who brings tidings); or ن-ب-و (n-b-w) — to be high or elevated (one of exalted rank), favoured by those who note the doubled yāʾ pointing to an original wāw.

3.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
3.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.
3.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

4.meaning: "to/for your wives" — azwāj is the plural of zawj, which means one of a matched pair, and so a spouse: husband or wife, the partner who completes a pair. With the preposition it means "to" or "for" one's spouses.

parts.en: spouses, wives, partners (plural of zawj, "one of a pair")

4.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition li- and carrying a possessive pronoun. The -i ending is the genitive, the case a noun must take after a preposition — it is li- that puts azwāj in the genitive. A joined possessive pronoun does not by itself cause this: in a possessive (iḍāfa) construction it is the following possessor that must be genitive, while the possessed noun keeps whatever case its own role in the sentence calls for (kitābu-ka, "your book", takes nominative -u when it is the subject). The suffix -ka means "your", addressing one male person.
4.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — to pair, to join two things as a couple

5.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
5.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

6.meaning: "you (women) were" — the past tense of kāna, the verb of simply being. It states that something was the case, and when placed before another present-form verb it shifts that verb into the past, giving the sense "you used to…" or "you were doing…".

parts.en: was, were (past stem of kāna, "to be")

6.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb. The long ā of kāna shortens to kun- whenever a consonant-beginning subject ending is attached. That ending, -tunna, marks the subject as second person, feminine, plural — a group of women being addressed, "you women". Besides meaning "were", this verb commonly works as a linking verb ("X was Y") and as a helper forming continuous or habitual past.
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, to exist

7.meaning: "you (women) want" — from arāda: to want, wish, desire, or intend something; it carries the sense of a purposeful will aimed at an outcome, not just a passing feeling.

parts.en: you (2nd person prefix, form IV pattern)

7.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb of the causative form IV pattern (arāda). The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject; the -na ending makes that subject feminine plural, "you women". The long vowel of the stem (turīd-) shortens to -rid- because the -na ending creates a consonant cluster. Note that feminine-plural verbs ending in -na keep exactly this shape in every mood, so the same word serves as statement, and after a governing particle as subjunctive or jussive.
7.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, go after, aim for

8.meaning: "the life" — the state of being alive; living existence, vitality.
8.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -a ending (on the feminine -t) is accusative, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb or the noun governed by certain particles.

9.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
9.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
9.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

10.meaning: And its adornment / its finery. 'zīna' is decoration, ornament, beauty, or the attractive splendour with which something is made appealing. The attached pronoun makes it 'its adornment'; the leading 'wa' means 'and'.
10.grammar: A feminine noun with 'wa' ('and') in front and the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her') at the end. The '-a' ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case marking a noun that is the object of a verb or otherwise governed in that role. The '-hā' shows possession by a feminine or grammatically feminine thing: 'its adornment'.

11.meaning: "then come!" — a summons, literally "come up here", built from the sense of height: the one calling invites others to come toward him. It is the ordinary Arabic way of saying "come here!" and often introduces an offer or proposal.

parts.en: then, so (linking what follows to what came before)
come! (imperative of taʿālā, "to come up, come over")

11.grammar: A command (imperative) verb with the connecting particle fa- in front, which links it to a preceding statement as its consequence or next step. The -ayna ending is the feminine-plural addressee marker: the command is directed at a group of women, "come, all of you". Commands carry no case ending; this ending shows only who is being addressed.
11.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — height, elevation, to be high

12.meaning: "I will give you provision" — from mattaʿa (form II of the root for enjoyment): to grant someone something to enjoy and benefit from, to furnish them with goods or a gift, especially a parting settlement given to a woman on separation.

parts.en: give enjoyment, provide, furnish with goods

12.grammar: An imperfect verb of the doubled (form II) pattern, which makes the action something one does TO another: not "enjoy" but "cause to enjoy, provide for". The u- prefix means the subject is "I". The stem's last letter carries no vowel at all (…-tiʿ, not -tiʿu), which marks the jussive mood — the form used after particles like lam and lā of prohibition, and for the result-clause of a condition ("then I will provide for you"). The -kunna suffix is the object: a group of women, "you women".
12.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — enjoyment, benefit, goods that give pleasure or use

13.meaning: "and I will release you" — from sarraḥa, whose base image is sending livestock out to open pasture; applied to people it means to let go, set free, dismiss, and specifically to release a wife from marriage.

parts.en: release, let go, set free, send away

13.grammar: An imperfect verb of the doubled (form II) pattern, which makes it transitive and deliberate: to send someone off. The u- prefix means "I". The stem ends with no vowel on its final letter (-riḥ, not -riḥu), marking the jussive mood, used after particles such as lam and lā of prohibition and in the result-clause of a condition. The suffix -kunna is the object pronoun for a group of women.
13.root: س-ر-ح (s-r-ḥ) — to send out to pasture, let loose, set free

14.meaning: "a releasing, a setting free" — the verbal noun of sarraḥa: the act itself of letting go or dismissing, and in the matter of marriage a formal release or separation. As a verbal noun it is often added to its own verb to stress or qualify the manner of the action ("release you with a fine release").

parts.en: accusative ending with indefinite marker ("a release")

14.grammar: A masculine verbal noun (the noun that names an action). The doubled n-sound of -an marks it indefinite, and the -a vowel is accusative — the case a noun takes as the object of a verb, and characteristically the case of a verbal noun placed beside its own verb to emphasise or describe the way the action is done.
14.root: س-ر-ح (s-r-ḥ) — to send out to pasture, let loose, set free

15.meaning: Beautiful, gracious, handsome — of pleasing quality in conduct, appearance, or manner; when describing patience or forbearance it indicates dignified, uncomplaining, and noble bearing.
15.grammar: Adjective of the intensive pattern faʿīl. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, agreeing with the preceding accusative noun it qualifies (an adjective in Arabic follows and agrees with its noun in case, number, gender, and definiteness).
15.root: ج-م-ل (j-m-l) — to be beautiful, to be gracious, to be fine

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: "you (women) were" — the past tense of kāna, the verb of simply being. It states that something was the case, and when placed before another present-form verb it shifts that verb into the past, giving the sense "you used to…" or "you were doing…".

parts.en: was, were (past stem of kāna, "to be")

2.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb. The long ā of kāna shortens to kun- whenever a consonant-beginning subject ending is attached. That ending, -tunna, marks the subject as second person, feminine, plural — a group of women being addressed, "you women". Besides meaning "were", this verb commonly works as a linking verb ("X was Y") and as a helper forming continuous or habitual past.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, to exist

3.meaning: "you (women) want" — from arāda: to want, wish, desire, or intend something; it carries the sense of a purposeful will aimed at an outcome, not just a passing feeling.

parts.en: you (2nd person prefix, form IV pattern)

3.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb of the causative form IV pattern (arāda). The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject; the -na ending makes that subject feminine plural, "you women". The long vowel of the stem (turīd-) shortens to -rid- because the -na ending creates a consonant cluster. Note that feminine-plural verbs ending in -na keep exactly this shape in every mood, so the same word serves as statement, and after a governing particle as subjunctive or jussive.
3.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, go after, aim for

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

5.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
5.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

6.meaning: "and the abode/home" — dār is a dwelling place, a home with its enclosure; used absolutely with "the" it names a whole realm of dwelling, an abode considered as a permanent place of residence.
6.grammar: A definite singular feminine noun. The l of al- assimilates in pronunciation to the following d, giving "ad-dār". The -a ending is the accusative, which generally marks the noun as the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or as governed by a verb-like particle, as opposed to being the subject.
6.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn or go around; hence dār, the enclosure one's life circles within

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come' — literally 'the last (abode)', the final, everlasting existence following this present life.
7.grammar: A definite noun (al- = 'the') bearing the -a ending, which marks the accusative (object) case — the form a noun takes when it is the object of a verb. It is feminine in form (the tā' marbūṭa ending).
7.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after; lastness, the end

8.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
8.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
9.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

10.meaning: He has prepared / made ready — to set something up in advance, to ready or get it in order beforehand.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he prepared'). It belongs to the 'form IV' pattern (the a- prefix gives the sense of actively making something ready). With no added subject suffix, the bare form means 'he' did the action, completed in the past. The doubled middle letter (shadda) is part of this root.
10.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — to count, prepare, make ready

11.meaning: "for the women who do good" — muḥsināt are those who act with iḥsān: doing what is good, and doing it beautifully and thoroughly, going beyond bare duty to excellence. The feminine plural names such women; with the preposition it means "for" or "belonging to" them.

parts.en: one who does good and does it well

11.grammar: An active participle (the "one who does X" form) of the causative form IV, made definite and put in the sound feminine plural with -āt. The final -i is the genitive ending, required after the preposition li-. In sound feminine plurals this single -i ending covers both the genitive and the accusative, so only the surrounding words show which one is meant. The article al- loses its a after li-, giving lil-.
11.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — beauty, goodness, doing something well

12.meaning: "from among you (women)" — the preposition min, which marks a source, a starting point, or a part taken out of a whole, joined to the pronoun for a group of women; so "out of you", "from among your number".

parts.en: from, out of, among (part of a whole)

12.grammar: A preposition with a joined pronoun. Min takes whatever follows it in the genitive; pronouns show no visible case ending, so the pronoun simply attaches directly. The suffix -kunna specifies second person, feminine, plural — a group of women being addressed. One core use of min is partitive: singling out some members out of a larger group.

13.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
13.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
13.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

14.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
14.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: "O wives!" — a direct call, in the construct shape "O wives of …". Nisāʾ is the general plural for women, and when linked to a man it means his wives; it is also used for the female members of a household or community.

parts.en: O (particle used to call or address someone)

1.grammar: A vocative construction: yā is the particle for calling out to someone. A single-word person addressed directly would take the plain -u ending, but when the called noun governs a following noun ("O wives OF …") it takes the accusative -a instead — the ending this form carries. So the -a signals that the call is joined to a following possessor.
1.root: ن-س-و (n-s-w) — womanhood, the female. Nisāʾ is an irregular (broken) plural with no singular built from this root; the gap is filled by imraʾah, "a woman", which comes from the unrelated root م-ر-أ (m-r-ʾ) — a stand-in singular of this kind is called suppletive.

2.meaning: The Prophet — a person who receives revelation from Allah and announces it, one given prophetic news and inspired tidings from the unseen.
2.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'the'. The final -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive chain, follows a preposition, or marks agreement with a preceding genitive word. The article's l assimilates into the following n (an-nabiy), since n is a 'sun letter'.
2.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; to inform, announce

3.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
3.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
3.root: — (pronoun)

4.meaning: He/it comes, or brings. From the verb 'to come'; with an object it carries the sense of bringing or producing something.
4.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 3rd person masculine. This root ends weakly in a vowel, and the bare form yati (without a final -ī) shows the jussive or apocopated mood, the clipped form used after conditional particles and in answers to conditions.

5.meaning: "from among you (women)" — the preposition min, which marks a source, a starting point, or a part taken out of a whole, joined to the pronoun for a group of women; so "out of you", "from among your number".

parts.en: from, out of, among (part of a whole)

5.grammar: A preposition with a joined pronoun. Min takes whatever follows it in the genitive; pronouns show no visible case ending, so the pronoun simply attaches directly. The suffix -kunna specifies second person, feminine, plural — a group of women being addressed. One core use of min is partitive: singling out some members out of a larger group.

6.meaning: A noun preceded by 'with,' built on the word for a gross indecency — an outrageous, shameful, morally excessive act; sexual immorality or any flagrant transgression.
6.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The tāʾ marbūṭa (-at) marks it as a feminine singular noun denoting the act itself. The final -in (tanwīn kasra) is the indefinite genitive ending ('a …'), the case regularly required after a preposition.
6.root: ف-ح-ش (f-ḥ-sh) — gross indecency, excess, shamefulness

7.meaning: An adjective meaning 'made clear, manifest, plainly evident' — describing something that has been openly shown or is unmistakable.
7.grammar: An active participle of the intensive form-II pattern (mubayyina), meaning 'one that makes clear / is manifest.' The mu- prefix forms the participle; the -at marks feminine agreement; the final -in (tanwīn kasra) is the indefinite genitive — the case used to agree with a preceding genitive noun or after a preposition.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness, making plain

8.meaning: It will be doubled, multiplied over and over — made to grow in repeated increments rather than simply added once.
8.grammar: Passive present-tense verb, 'it'. The yu- prefix with the internal a-vowels marks the passive voice: the subject has the doubling done TO it. The vowel-less (sukūn) ending marks the jussive mood, the form a verb takes in the result of a condition ('whoever ... , it will be doubled').

9.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
9.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

10.meaning: "the punishment / torment" — a painful penalty or chastisement inflicted as retribution; suffering imposed as a consequence.
10.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a verb or the doer/topic of a sentence.

11.meaning: Twofold, double, or two times over — twice the usual amount.
11.grammar: A dual noun (referring to exactly two). The '-ayni' ending marks the dual in the accusative/genitive — the special form Arabic uses for a pair, here meaning 'a double, twice as much'.
11.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — to double, multiply; a multiple, fold

12.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence

13.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
13.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

14.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
14.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
14.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: 'Easy, effortless, slight, manageable.' It describes something simple to do or small in amount.
16.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('an easy …'), commonly marking an adjective agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or a verb's object/complement.
16.root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — to be easy, light, manageable

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: "he/she is devoutly obedient" — from qanata: to submit humbly and steadily, to be devout and compliant in worship and obedience, standing in willing service rather than mere outward compliance.

parts.en: he / it (3rd person masculine singular prefix)

2.grammar: An imperfect (present-form) verb, third person masculine singular, "he". Its final letter carries no vowel (-nut, not -nutu), which marks the jussive mood: the form required after particles like lam ("did not") and lā of prohibition, and in both halves of a conditional sentence after words such as in and man ("whoever").
2.root: ق-ن-ت (q-n-t) — devout obedience, humble and constant submission

3.meaning: "from among you (women)" — the preposition min, which marks a source, a starting point, or a part taken out of a whole, joined to the pronoun for a group of women; so "out of you", "from among your number".

parts.en: from, out of, among (part of a whole)

3.grammar: A preposition with a joined pronoun. Min takes whatever follows it in the genitive; pronouns show no visible case ending, so the pronoun simply attaches directly. The suffix -kunna specifies second person, feminine, plural — a group of women being addressed. One core use of min is partitive: singling out some members out of a larger group.

4.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
4.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
5.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
5.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

6.meaning: "and he/she does" — from ʿamila: to do, to work, to act, to put something into practice. It refers to deeds actually carried out rather than intentions or words.
6.grammar: An imperfect verb; the ta- prefix marks either "she" (third person feminine singular) or "you" (second person masculine singular) — the surrounding words decide which. The final letter carries no vowel (-mal, not -malu), marking the jussive mood, used after lam and lā of prohibition and in conditional sentences.
6.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to work, to do, to act

7.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
7.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
7.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

8.meaning: "We give her" — from ātā (the causative of "to come"): to make something come to someone, that is, to give, hand over, or bestow. It is a plain verb of granting, whether reward, wealth, or knowledge.
8.grammar: An imperfect verb of the causative form IV. The nu- prefix means the subject is "we". The stem ends in a weak letter that would normally be a long -ī (nuʾtī); it is shortened to -i, and that shortening is exactly how weak-ending verbs show the jussive mood — the form used after lam and lā of prohibition and in the result-clause of a condition ("…then We give her"). The suffix -hā is the object, "her/it", for something grammatically feminine.
8.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in form IV, to make come, to give

9.meaning: "her reward" — ajr is the wage, recompense, or payment earned for work done; it covers both a worker's hire and the reward Allah gives for deeds, always with the sense of something due in return for effort.
9.grammar: A masculine singular noun with a joined possessive pronoun. The -a before the pronoun is the accusative, which generally marks a noun as the object of a verb — the thing given, made, or acted upon. The suffix -hā means "her" or "its", referring back to a feminine singular owner, so the noun stands in a possessive relation ("the reward OF her").
9.root: أ-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — wage, hire, recompense for work

10.meaning: Two times, twice — exactly two occurrences of something. It is the dual ('exactly two') form of the noun meaning 'a time/instance'.
10.grammar: A dual noun, meaning 'exactly two' of the thing. The -ayni ending marks the dual in the accusative or genitive state; for an adverb of frequency this conveys 'two times / twice'. Arabic has a special dual distinct from the plural (three or more).
10.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — to pass by; a passing, hence an instance/time

11.meaning: And We have made ready — to prepare, arrange, and set something in store beforehand so it stands waiting.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb (form VIII) prefixed with 'wa' (and). The 't' in the stem is the form VIII infix, not a root letter. The suffix '-nā' is the subject ending meaning 'we (did it),' marking a completed action performed by a first-person plural — an act already accomplished.
11.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — counting, reckoning; readying and setting in store (form VIII اعتدّ, with the doubled dāl, from this root)

12.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
12.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.
12.root: — (preposition + pronoun)

13.meaning: 'provision,' 'sustenance,' 'a means of livelihood' — that which is bestowed to sustain and benefit, such as food and resources. 'Rizq' is whatever Allah grants a creature to live on, material or otherwise.
13.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case with indefiniteness — frequently the role of a stated purpose or explanatory complement ('as provision'), telling for what reason or in what capacity something is given.

14.meaning: Noble, generous, honourable — describing something or someone of high worth, dignity, and openhanded goodness. Used of provision, status, or character that is precious and held in honour.
14.grammar: An adjective in the indefinite accusative. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks the indefinite accusative case, which typically signals the object of a verb or a descriptive/adverbial role, in an unspecified, non-particular sense ('a noble/generous one').

1.meaning: "O wives!" — a direct call, in the construct shape "O wives of …". Nisāʾ is the general plural for women, and when linked to a man it means his wives; it is also used for the female members of a household or community.

parts.en: O (particle used to call or address someone)

1.grammar: A vocative construction: yā is the particle for calling out to someone. A single-word person addressed directly would take the plain -u ending, but when the called noun governs a following noun ("O wives OF …") it takes the accusative -a instead — the ending this form carries. So the -a signals that the call is joined to a following possessor.
1.root: ن-س-و (n-s-w) — womanhood, the female. Nisāʾ is an irregular (broken) plural with no singular built from this root; the gap is filled by imraʾah, "a woman", which comes from the unrelated root م-ر-أ (m-r-ʾ) — a stand-in singular of this kind is called suppletive.

2.meaning: The Prophet — a person who receives revelation from Allah and announces it, one given prophetic news and inspired tidings from the unseen.
2.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'the'. The final -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive chain, follows a preposition, or marks agreement with a preceding genitive word. The article's l assimilates into the following n (an-nabiy), since n is a 'sun letter'.
2.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; to inform, announce

3.meaning: "you (women) are not" — the negative counterpart of "to be": it denies that the subject is or has some quality at present. English needs "are not" or "is not", but Arabic expresses this with a verb of its own.

parts.en: is not, are not (stem of laysa, negation of being)

3.grammar: A defective verb: it is shaped like a past-tense verb but always negates in the present. The -tunna ending marks the subject as second person, feminine, plural — a group of women, "you women are not". Like kāna, it takes a subject and then a complement naming what is being denied of that subject, and that complement stands in the accusative.
3.root: ل-ي-س (l-y-s) — negation, "there is not"; a defective verb with no full family of derived words

4.meaning: "like any one" — the preposition ka, marking likeness or comparison, joined to aḥad, which means "one" and, in comparisons and negations, "anyone at all", "a single one". Together: resembling any single one of a kind.

parts.en: genitive ending with indefinite marker ("any one")

4.grammar: A preposition attached directly to an indefinite noun. The -in ending does two jobs: the doubled n-sound marks the noun indefinite, and the -i vowel is the genitive, which is what every noun must take after a preposition such as ka-. Aḥad is especially at home after a negation, where it means "not a single one".
4.root: أ-ح-د (ʾ-ḥ-d) — oneness, being single or unique

5.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
5.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

6.meaning: 'The women' — the plural used for women/females collectively. (It serves as the plural of mar'a, 'woman.')
6.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or standing in a possessive ('of …') relationship. The l of al- assimilates into the following n in pronunciation (a 'sun letter').
6.root: ن-س-و / ن-س-ء (n-s-w / n-s-') — women / womankind

7.meaning: If — a particle introducing a condition: it sets up 'if X (happens), then Y'.
7.grammar: A conditional particle ('if') that introduces a supposed case and typically puts the following verb into the jussive (conditional) form. Its base shape is 'in', whose final nūn carries a sukūn and is fully pronounced. When the next word begins with a sukūn-bearing cluster, the otherwise-quiescent nūn is given a kasra (-i) to avoid two consecutive sukūns meeting (the 'meeting of two quiescents'); this helping vowel eases pronunciation and carries no grammatical meaning of its own.

8.meaning: "you (women) guarded yourselves / were mindful of Allah" — the verb of taqwā. Its root sense is to shield or protect oneself from harm; used of a person before Allah it means to keep a careful, reverent guard on one's conduct, avoiding what displeases Him out of awareness of Him.

parts.en: prefixed vowel of the form VIII pattern ("guard oneself")
guarded oneself, was mindful of Allah

8.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb of form VIII, the pattern that turns an action back on the doer: not "protect" but "protect oneself". The -tunna ending marks the subject as second person, feminine, plural, "you women". The stem's weak final letter shows up as -ay- before this consonant-beginning ending. A past-tense verb of this kind also serves as the verb of a conditional clause, reading as "if you guard yourselves".
8.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect from harm

9.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
9.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

10.meaning: "you (women) are soft/yielding" — from khaḍaʿa, to lower or bend down, hence to be submissive, pliant, and soft. Used of speech it means to drop the voice into a soft, coaxing, alluring tone.

parts.en: be soft, lower oneself, be yielding

10.grammar: An imperfect verb; the ta- prefix marks a second-person subject and the -na ending makes it feminine plural, "you women". Feminine-plural verbs of this shape are fixed: they look identical whether the sense is a plain statement, a subjunctive, or a jussive, so a preceding particle — for instance lā of prohibition, giving "do not be soft" — is what supplies the mood.
10.root: خ-ض-ع (kh-ḍ-ʿ) — to lower, bend down, be submissive

11.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with/by the saying' or 'with the word/statement'. It combines the preposition 'bi-' (with, by means of) with 'al-qawl', a verbal noun meaning an act of speech, an utterance, a statement, or a word that is spoken.
11.grammar: A preposition ('bi-', with/by) attached to a definite noun. The preposition forces the genitive case, which is why the noun ends in '-i' rather than '-u'. The '-i' ending here is the mark of a noun governed by a preposition, conveying the sense 'with the saying' or 'by means of the word'.
11.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

12.meaning: "so that he may covet" — from ṭamiʿa: to be filled with eager, greedy desire for something, to set one's hopes on getting it. It suggests appetite roused by the expectation that the thing is within reach.

parts.en: so that, and then (marking a result or consequence)
covet, desire greedily, set hopes on

12.grammar: An imperfect verb, third person masculine singular, "he". The final -a ending is the subjunctive, the mood of purpose and consequence: it appears after particles such as an, lan and kay, and after the fa- that introduces a result following a command or prohibition — hence the sense "so that he would…", "with the result that he might…".
12.root: ط-م-ع (ṭ-m-ʿ) — greed, eager craving, covetous hope

13.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
13.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
14.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

15.meaning: 'His heart' — the heart as the inner seat of thought, feeling, intention, and faith.
15.grammar: A noun ('heart') with the possessive pronoun -hi ('his') attached. The -i before the pronoun marks the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or as the second part of a possessive pair. (The pronoun is voweled -hi rather than -hu to harmonize with the preceding -i sound.)

16.meaning: "an illness" — maraḍ is sickness or disease: a disorder that spoils sound functioning. It is used of bodily illness and equally of a sickness in the heart — corrupt desire, doubt, or moral disease.

parts.en: nominative ending with indefinite marker ("an illness")

16.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -un ending combines two markers: the doubled n-sound shows the noun is indefinite, "an illness", and the -u vowel is the nominative, the case that generally marks the subject of a sentence — the one doing or being something, or the thing whose existence is being asserted.
16.root: م-ر-ض (m-r-ḍ) — illness, sickness, whether of body or of heart

17.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they (women) said' — to utter or speak. The form encodes a group of females as the speakers, joined to what precedes by 'and'.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb. The attached '-na' ending marks the subject as a group of females ('they', women), so the action is completed and done by multiple female actors. The 'wa-' prefix simply connects it with 'and'.

18.meaning: 'A saying / word / statement' — an utterance or speech; that which is said.
18.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'a saying.' The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥ): it marks an indefinite noun in the accusative case, the form used for the object of a verb (e.g., 'to say a word') among other roles.

19.meaning: 'Honorable / fitting / recognized as good' — that which is known and accepted by sound custom and conscience as right and decent. A loaded ethical term: the commonly acknowledged good, the opposite of munkar (the rejected/wrong).
19.grammar: A passive participle on the mafʿūl pattern, literally 'that which is known/recognized,' hence 'what is recognized as fitting and good.' The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥ), the form an indefinite noun/adjective takes as an object or in agreement with one.

1.meaning: A command addressed to a group of women: "settle down, stay put, remain at rest." The verb carries the sense of coming to a standstill in a place and being content there rather than moving restlessly about — the opposite of roaming or being unsettled.

parts.en: settle / remain at rest (shortened imperative stem)

1.grammar: An imperative (a direct command). Verbs never take case endings; the final -na is itself the 2nd person feminine plural subject pronoun, so the command is spoken to several women together ("you women, do this"), and a verb carrying this -na is fixed in shape. The stem is shortened: from the doubled root one of the identical letters is dropped, giving qar- instead of the fuller iqrar-/iqrir- (some grammarians instead derive this fatḥa-vowelled shape from the root w-q-r, "to be grave and settled"). The wa- at the front simply joins the command to a preceding clause.
1.root: ق-ر-ر (q-r-r) — to settle, be firmly at rest, remain in place (also coolness, stability)

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

3.meaning: "The houses of you (women)" — dwellings, homes; a bayt is a place one spends the night, a household and living space, not merely a building.
3.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun carrying a possessive pronoun. The -i ending is genitive: the case used after a preposition and in "the X of Y" links. The suffix -kunna means "your" addressed to a group of females (as against -kum for males or mixed groups). Because a pronoun is attached, the noun counts as definite and takes no -n (tanwīn).
3.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to pass the night; a dwelling, home

4.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
4.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

5.meaning: To flaunt oneself — to make one's beauty, finery and adornment conspicuous and put it on show before others. The image behind the word is of something rising up prominently so that it cannot be missed; used of deliberate, attention-seeking display of one's charms.

parts.en: Form V prefix: do the act to/for oneself

5.grammar: A Form V verb: the ta- prefix plus the doubled middle root letter give a reflexive-intensive sense, "to make one's own self conspicuous." The final -na is the feminine plural subject pronoun, so the verb speaks of or to several women; a verb with this -na is fixed in shape and takes no case vowel. The written form is ambiguous in itself: it can be a past tense ("they/you women flaunted themselves"), a 2nd person feminine plural imperative ("flaunt yourselves"), or — when one of two identical tā's is dropped — a present-tense jussive used in prohibitions ("do not flaunt yourselves").
5.root: ب-ر-ج (b-r-j) — prominence, a tower; to stand out conspicuously

6.meaning: The act of flaunting itself — ostentatious display of one's beauty and adornment, showing off so as to draw eyes. As a verbal noun it names the behaviour as a thing ("a flaunting, a parading of finery").

parts.en: prefix of the Form V verbal noun ("the act of …-ing oneself")

6.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) of a Form V verb, on the pattern tafaʿʿul: instead of naming who acts, it names the action itself. The final vowel is a bare -a, the accusative case, and the absence of the -n sound (tanwīn) shows the noun is not indefinite — this shape occurs when the noun is the first term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa), joined to a following noun that completes it ("the flaunting of …"). Accusative is the case of a verb's object, of the "absolute object" that echoes and intensifies a verb of the same root, and of adverbial expressions of manner.
6.root: ب-ر-ج (b-r-j) — prominence, a tower; to stand out conspicuously

7.meaning: Pre-Islamic ignorance — the state and outlook of heedless, godless ignorance, especially the customs, pride, and false beliefs of the age before guidance. An abstract noun for that condition of unenlightenment.
7.grammar: A definite abstract noun formed with the -iyya suffix (which turns a word into a named state or "-ism"), here ending in -i, which is genitive. This ending typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… OF …") or follows a preposition.
7.root: ج-ه-ل (j-h-l) — ignorance, not knowing; also reckless, hot-headed behavior

8.meaning: The first, the foremost, the initial one — the feminine form of the ordinal 'first', denoting that which comes before all others in order or time.
8.grammar: A definite ordinal adjective (with al-, 'the'), the feminine of 'first', so it describes a feminine noun. It ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case; it conveys priority in sequence ('the first/former').
8.root: ا-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to precede, origin

9.meaning: "And set up / establish" — a command to a group of women. The Form IV verb means to make something stand upright, hence to put a thing in place properly and keep it going; with acts of worship it means to perform them fully and steadily, not merely to go through the motions.
9.grammar: A Form IV imperative: the a- prefix makes the basic sense "stand" causative — "make stand, establish." The weak middle root letter is dropped in this shortened command shape. Verbs take no case endings; the final -na is the 2nd person feminine plural subject pronoun, addressing several women together and leaving the verb fixed in form.
9.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright

10.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
10.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

11.meaning: "And give / hand over" — a command to a group of women. Literally "cause to come to (someone)": to bring a thing to another and put it in their hands, hence to give, render, or pay what is due.

parts.en: give / hand over (Form IV imperative stem)

11.grammar: A Form IV imperative from a root that begins with hamza and ends in a weak letter. The long ā (written with the madda sign) is the result of the Form IV causative hamza prefix merging with the root's own initial hamza — the causative sense being "make come," i.e. give. The weak final root letter reappears as -ī before the ending. Verbs take no case vowel; the closing -na is the 2nd person feminine plural subject pronoun, so several women are addressed together.
11.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive (Form IV: to make come, i.e. to give)

12.meaning: The purifying alms (zakāt) — the obligatory portion given from one's wealth that purifies it and causes it to grow; an act of worship and social due.
12.grammar: A definite feminine noun (the tied tā' marks the feminine). The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the alms').
12.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure; to grow, increase, be blessed

13.meaning: "And obey" — a command to a group of women. The verb implies willing, ready compliance offered from the heart, not compliance extracted by force; to fall in with another's word gladly.
13.grammar: A Form IV imperative; the weak middle root letter is dropped in this shortened command stem. Verbs carry no case endings, and the final -na is the 2nd person feminine plural subject pronoun, so the order is addressed to several women together and the verb stays fixed in shape.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
14.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

15.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
15.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

16.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
16.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

17.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
17.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
17.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

19.meaning: "So that He may take away / remove." The Form IV verb means to cause something to go off and depart, hence to make it disappear, strip it away, or clear it off entirely.
19.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb. The yu- prefix marks a third person masculine singular subject ("he/it"), and its u-vowel is the sign of the Form IV causative pattern ("make go" rather than simply "go"); the pattern's hamza, present in the past tense, drops out in the present. The prefixed li- expresses purpose ("in order that") and puts the verb in the subjunctive, which is why the final vowel is -a rather than the -u of a plain statement.
19.root: ذ-ه-ب (dh-h-b) — to go, depart, pass away

20.meaning: From you (plural) — ʿan is the preposition 'from/away from', and -kumu is the second-person masculine plural possessive/objective pronoun.

parts.en: 2nd person masculine plural pronoun suffix: you (plural)

20.grammar: ʿAn is a preposition governing the pronoun. The plural suffix -kum takes a helping vowel -u when followed by another word. The whole phrase functions as an adverbial complement meaning 'from/away from you all'.
20.root: — (ʿan is a preposition particle; no triliteral root)

21.meaning: A noun meaning 'filth', 'defilement', or 'abomination' — that which is impure, foul, or repugnant, whether physically unclean or spiritually corrupting.
21.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- (its 'l' assimilated into the following 'r', producing 'r-rijs'). The -a (accusative) ending typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

22.meaning: People of / folk of — the people belonging to something, its members or family; those who hold or are associated with a thing (a place, a faith, a household).
22.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/folk of …,' normally joined to a following noun ('the people OF …'). The final -a (fatḥa) is the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or after certain particles.
22.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, people belonging to something

23.meaning: Al-bayt — the house, dwelling, or home; a place of residence or a building set apart, often used for a household or a place of worship.
23.grammar: A definite noun. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle. The word denotes a house, dwelling, or set-apart sacred building.
23.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night; house, dwelling

24.meaning: "And that He may purify you" — to cleanse thoroughly, to make pure and free of filth, whether outward dirt or inward taint such as sin and blameworthy character.

parts.en: you (object pronoun, a group of males or a mixed group)

24.grammar: A present-tense Form II verb: the doubled middle root letter makes the action intensive and transitive — not just "be pure" but "make thoroughly pure." The yu- prefix marks a third person masculine singular subject ("he/it"). The -a is the subjunctive ending, the form a present verb takes after a particle of purpose or intent ("so that …"). The object pronoun -kum ("you," plural, males or a mixed group) attaches directly after that ending, so the whole word means "and that He may purify you."
24.root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r) — purity, cleanness, freedom from filth

25.meaning: A purifying — the act of cleansing thoroughly, named as a thing in itself. Because it comes from the intensive pattern, it conveys a complete, deep cleansing rather than a light rinse.

parts.en: prefix of the Form II verbal noun ("the act of …-ing")

25.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) of a Form II verb, on the pattern tafʿīl, naming the action rather than the doer. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative — the -n sound (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite, "a purifying." Accusative verbal nouns of this shape typically serve as the "absolute object" reinforcing a verb of the same root, the Arabic way of saying an action was done thoroughly and unmistakably.
25.root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r) — purity, cleanness, freedom from filth

1.meaning: "And remember / call to mind / mention aloud" — a command to a group of women. The verb covers both inward recollection (keeping something present in the mind and heart) and outward mention with the tongue.

parts.en: connecting alif: helping vowel that starts the command

1.grammar: A basic (Form I) imperative. Because the stem begins with two consonants, a helping vowel (hamzat al-waṣl) is prefixed to make it pronounceable, taking u- to match the stem's u-vowel; that vowel drops in pronunciation when a word precedes it, so wa + udhkur is read wadhkur. Verbs take no case endings; the final -na is the 2nd person feminine plural subject pronoun, addressing several women together and leaving the verb fixed in shape.

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: It is recited / read aloud — a passage of revelation is being conveyed by being read out.
3.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('it is being recited'). The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive (no doer named), and the final weak -ā shows it derives from a root ending in a weak letter; it conveys an ongoing action done to the subject.
3.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: "The houses of you (women)" — dwellings, homes; a bayt is a place one spends the night, a household and living space, not merely a building.
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun carrying a possessive pronoun. The -i ending is genitive: the case used after a preposition and in "the X of Y" links. The suffix -kunna means "your" addressed to a group of females (as against -kum for males or mixed groups). Because a pronoun is attached, the noun counts as definite and takes no -n (tanwīn).
5.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to pass the night; a dwelling, home

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
6.root: — (preposition)

7.meaning: Signs / verses / evidentiary marks — the plural of 'āyah', a sign or token that points to something beyond itself; used for miraculous signs, natural wonders, and the discrete verses of revelation.
7.grammar: A sound feminine plural. The '-in' (nunation) ending marks it as indefinite ('signs', not 'the signs') and is the genitive/accusative (oblique) case form, typical of an object or a word governed by a preposition.
7.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token that indicates something

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: And the wisdom — sound judgment, deep understanding, and the placing of things rightly; knowledge joined to right action. It often denotes Allah-given insight or the wise content of revelation.
9.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the definite article 'the' attached to a feminine singular noun ('wisdom'). The -i ending is genitive, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

10.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
10.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
11.root: — (proper name)

12.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

12.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

13.meaning: Subtle and finely gentle: so delicate as to be imperceptible, reaching into the smallest hidden details, and gracious in a quiet, unnoticed way. Of Allah it combines two ideas — knowledge that penetrates to the most minute and concealed things, and kindness that reaches His servants by means too fine for them to detect.

parts.en: subtle, finely gentle, penetrating in kindness

13.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which describes a settled, characteristic quality rather than a passing act. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative: the -n sound (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite ("subtle," not "the subtle one"), and the accusative case is used for the object of a verb and for the predicate that follows verbs of being such as kāna ("… was/is subtle").

14.meaning: All-Aware — one who knows things from the inside, with intimate, penetrating knowledge of hidden realities; as a name of Allah, the One fully acquainted with the inner truth of everything.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, signaling a permanent, thorough quality: not merely informed but deeply and constantly aware. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, the case commonly taken by a description completing a verb or by the second part of an 'ask/find X to be Y' construction.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The ones who submit/surrender — those who give themselves wholly to Allah in willing obedience and peace (the Muslims). As an active participle it names people characterized by this submission.
2.grammar: The prefix al- is 'the'. The stem is the Form IV active participle 'one who submits/surrenders'. The ending -īna is the sound masculine plural in the genitive/accusative state (the form used after prepositions, as object, or when linked to a preceding noun); its nominative counterpart would be -ūna. So: 'the ones who submit'.

3.meaning: "And the women who submit" — Muslim women: those who hand themselves over wholly to Allah and so enter safety and peace. The root joins the ideas of wholeness, soundness and peace with the act of surrendering something intact into another's hands.

parts.en: the (its a- drops in pronunciation after wa, giving wal-)
one who submits / surrenders (Form IV doer)

3.grammar: An active participle (the "doer" noun) of a Form IV verb, made feminine plural. In the regular feminine plural, -ātu marks the subject case while the single form -āti covers both the object case and the genitive; so the -āti ending shown signals a non-subject role — typically after a preposition, in an "of" link, or as the object of a verb. The definite article al- makes it "the …" and blocks any final -n (tanwīn).
3.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — wholeness, soundness, peace; to hand over intact

4.meaning: "And the believing men" — those who have faith: they hold something to be true with inner trust, and so find security in it and give security to others. The root ties faith to safety and trust rather than to bare opinion.

parts.en: the (its a- drops after wa, giving wal-)
one who believes / entrusts (Form IV doer)

4.grammar: An active participle of a Form IV verb in the regular masculine plural. That plural distinguishes case by its ending: -ūna when the word is the subject, and -īna when it is an object or stands in a genitive relation (after a preposition or in an "of" link). The ending shown is -īna, so it marks a non-subject role. The article al- makes it definite ("the believers").

5.meaning: And the believing women — the feminine plural of those who have faith, who place their trust and security in Allah and inwardly affirm the truth.
5.grammar: An active participle (one who believes) in the sound feminine plural. The prefix wa- means 'and'; al- is the definite article 'the'. The ending -āti is the sound feminine plural marker in its genitive or accusative form (the -i vowel rather than -u): it names a group of females and signals that the word is governed by a preceding preposition, oath, or verb, or is linked to a following noun.
5.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to have faith

6.meaning: And the devoutly obedient ones — those who stand in humble, sustained submission and devotion, constant in worship and obedience; 'the devout'.
6.grammar: A masculine active participle ('one who is devoutly obedient'), preceded by 'wa' ('and') and made definite by 'al-' ('the'), plural by '-īna'. The '-īna' form is the oblique plural, used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition. The root sense blends humble obedience with steady standing in devotion.
6.root: ق-ن-ت (q-n-t) — devout obedience, humble submission, constancy in worship

7.meaning: "And the devoutly obedient women" — those marked by qunūt: a humble, sustained obedience to Allah, standing long in worship with quiet submissiveness rather than obeying fitfully.

parts.en: the (its a- drops after wa, giving wal-)

7.grammar: An active participle ("the one who does X") of a basic Form I verb, put into the regular feminine plural. In that plural, -ātu marks the subject case while -āti serves for both the object case and the genitive; the -āti ending therefore signals a non-subject role, such as after a preposition or as a verb's object. The article al- makes it definite, so there is no final -n.
7.root: ق-ن-ت (q-n-t) — devout obedience, humble and sustained submission in worship

8.meaning: And the truthful ones — those who are honest and sincere, whose words and inner state match reality; 'the truthful'.
8.grammar: A masculine active participle ('one who is truthful'), preceded by the connector 'wa' ('and') and made definite by 'al-' ('the'), plural by '-īna'. The '-īna' form is the oblique plural, used when the noun serves as a direct object or follows a preposition.

9.meaning: "And the truthful women" — those whose speech matches reality and whose inward state matches their outward claim; sincere and honest, keeping their word and being true to it.

parts.en: the (its a- drops after wa; its l merges into the following ṣ, read waṣ-ṣ…)

9.grammar: An active participle of a Form I verb in the regular feminine plural. That plural uses -ātu for the subject case and the single form -āti for both the object case and the genitive, so the -āti ending here marks a non-subject role — after a preposition, in an "of" link, or as an object. The definite article al- rules out any final -n (tanwīn); in pronunciation its l assimilates into the following letter.
9.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truth, sincerity, correspondence of word and reality

10.meaning: 'And those who are patient / the steadfast' — people who endure hardship with calm, self-restrained perseverance, holding firm without complaint. Joined by 'and'.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and'), the definite article (its 'l' assimilated into the following sun letter 'ṣ'), the active participle 'one who is patient', and the sound masculine plural ending -īna. The active participle names the doer of the quality; the -īna ending marks the masculine plural in the genitive or accusative case.

11.meaning: "And the patiently enduring women" — those who hold themselves firm: restraining the self under hardship, persevering in duty, and keeping back from what is forbidden, without complaint or collapse.

parts.en: the (its a- drops after wa; its l merges into the following ṣ, read waṣ-ṣ…)

11.grammar: An active participle of a Form I verb in the regular feminine plural. The plural marks case by its ending: -ātu for the subject, and -āti covering both the object case and the genitive; so the -āti shown signals a non-subject role, such as following a preposition or serving as a verb's object. The article al- makes the word definite, hence no final -n.
11.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to restrain, hold fast, endure patiently

12.meaning: "And the humble men" — those brought low in awe: still, hushed and lowered before Allah's greatness, with the humility showing in body, voice and glance as well as in the heart.

parts.en: the (its a- drops after wa, giving wal-)

12.grammar: An active participle of a Form I verb in the regular masculine plural. This plural shows case in its ending: -ūna when the word is the subject of a sentence, and -īna when it is an object or linked in a genitive relation (after a preposition or in an "of" phrase). The ending here is -īna, so it marks a non-subject role. The article al- makes it definite.
12.root: خ-ش-ع (kh-sh-ʿ) — to lower oneself, become still and submissive in awe

13.meaning: "And the humble women" — those brought low in awe: quiet, lowered and submissive before Allah's greatness, the humility appearing outwardly as well as inwardly.

parts.en: the (its a- drops after wa, giving wal-)

13.grammar: An active participle of a Form I verb in the regular feminine plural. In that plural, -ātu marks the subject case while the one form -āti does duty for both the object case and the genitive; the -āti ending therefore signals a non-subject role — after a preposition, in an "of" link, or as an object. The article al- makes it definite, so no final -n is added.
13.root: خ-ش-ع (kh-sh-ʿ) — to lower oneself, become still and submissive in awe

14.meaning: "And the men who give charity" — those who hand over ṣadaqah, a freely given gift sought for Allah's sake. The word links giving to truthfulness: such spending is treated as proof that the giver's faith is sincere.

parts.en: the (its a- drops after wa, giving wal-)
one who takes the act on himself (Form V doer prefix)
give freely as charity / confirm as true

14.grammar: An active participle of a Form V verb: the muta- prefix with the doubled middle root letter gives the sense of taking the action upon oneself, i.e. voluntarily giving of one's own. It stands in the regular masculine plural, which distinguishes case by its ending: -ūna for the subject, -īna for an object or a genitive link (after a preposition or in an "of" phrase). The ending shown is -īna, marking a non-subject role; al- makes it definite.
14.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truth, sincerity (hence ṣadaqah, giving that proves faith true)

15.meaning: "And the women who give charity" — those who hand over ṣadaqah, a voluntary gift given for Allah's sake, spending that bears witness to the sincerity of their faith.

parts.en: the (its a- drops after wa, giving wal-)
one who takes the act on herself (Form V doer prefix)
give freely as charity / confirm as true

15.grammar: An active participle of a Form V verb (muta- plus the doubled middle letter = taking the action upon oneself, giving of one's own), in the regular feminine plural. That plural uses -ātu for the subject case and the single form -āti for both the object case and the genitive, so the -āti ending signals a non-subject role — after a preposition, in an "of" link, or as an object. The article al- makes it definite.
15.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truth, sincerity (hence ṣadaqah, giving that proves faith true)

16.meaning: "And the men who fast" — those who hold back and keep still: abstaining from food, drink and marital relations for Allah's sake, the outward restraint standing for an inward restraint of the whole self.

parts.en: the (its a- drops after wa; its l merges into the following ṣ, read waṣ-ṣ…)

16.grammar: An active participle of a Form I verb whose middle root letter is weak; that weak letter surfaces as a hamza (ʾ) in this doer pattern. It takes the regular masculine plural, which shows case in its ending: -ūna for the subject, and -īna for an object or a genitive relation (after a preposition or in an "of" phrase). The ending here is -īna, so a non-subject role is signalled; al- makes it definite.
16.root: ص-و-م (ṣ-w-m) — to abstain, hold back, keep still

17.meaning: "And the women who fast" — those who abstain and hold back: refraining from food, drink and marital relations for Allah's sake, an outward restraint that trains the whole self.

parts.en: the (its a- drops after wa; its l merges into the following ṣ, read waṣ-ṣ…)

17.grammar: An active participle of a Form I verb with a weak middle root letter, which surfaces as a hamza (ʾ) in this pattern, put into the regular feminine plural. In that plural, -ātu marks the subject case while -āti serves for both the object case and the genitive; the -āti ending therefore signals a non-subject role — after a preposition, in an "of" link, or as an object. The article al- makes it definite.
17.root: ص-و-م (ṣ-w-m) — to abstain, hold back, keep still

18.meaning: "And the men who guard" — keepers and preservers: those who watch over a thing carefully, protect it from loss or harm, and keep it intact within its proper limits (also used of committing something to memory, holding it safe in the mind).

parts.en: the (its a- drops after wa, giving wal-)
one who guards and preserves (doer noun)

18.grammar: An active participle of a Form I verb in the regular masculine plural. The plural ending carries the case: -ūna when the word is the subject of its sentence, -īna when it is an object or stands in a genitive relation (after a preposition or in an "of" phrase). The ending shown is -īna, marking a non-subject role. The article al- makes it definite, so no final -n (tanwīn) appears.
18.root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ) — to guard, preserve, keep safe

19.meaning: Their private parts — furūj is the plural of farj, literally an 'opening'; in the Qur'anic idiom, guarding the furūj means guarding one's chastity.
19.grammar: A broken plural (farj → furūj). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative case: the mark of the direct object, the thing the verb acts on ('guard THEIR private parts'). -hum is the attached possessive pronoun 'their' for a group of men (or a mixed group).

20.meaning: "And the guarding/safeguarding women" — women who keep watch over something and preserve it faithfully: guarding chastity, keeping a trust, memorising and preserving what has been entrusted to them. The word describes an ongoing, characteristic activity of protecting and keeping intact.
20.grammar: An active participle (a "doer" word: "one who guards") in the sound feminine plural, made definite by al- ("the ones who guard"). The -āt marks a plural of women; because al- is attached there is no -n (nunation) at the end. In the sound feminine plural the ending -i does double duty: it is the form used both for the object of a verb (accusative) and for the after-a-preposition / "…of…" relation (genitive) — only the -u ending would mark it as the subject.

21.meaning: "And the men who remember/mention" — those who keep Allah consciously in mind and on their tongues: recalling Him, invoking and praising Him habitually rather than once. The root covers both inward remembrance and outward mention.

parts.en: the (its l is absorbed into the following dh, hence dh-dh)
one who remembers, calls to mind, mentions

21.grammar: An active participle ("one who remembers") in the sound masculine plural with al- ("the ones who…"). The plural ending -īna is the form used when the word is the object of a verb (accusative) or is linked to a preceding preposition or to a following noun in an "…of…" relation (genitive); the alternative ending -ūna would instead mark it as the subject doing the action.
21.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembering, calling to mind, mentioning

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
22.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

23.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
23.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (the 'tanwīn' of fatḥa). The accusative case here commonly marks an object of a verb or an indefinite quantity; the doubled-n sound (nunation) signals that the word is indefinite ('many', not 'the many').
23.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

24.meaning: "And the women who remember/mention" — women characterised by keeping Allah in mind and on their tongues, invoking and praising Him as an ongoing habit.

parts.en: the (its l is absorbed into the following dh)
