24.grammar: An active participle in the sound feminine plural made definite by al-; -āt marks a plural of women, and al- explains why there is no final -n. For this plural pattern the single ending -i serves both as the object form (accusative) and as the form used after prepositions or in an "…of…" link (genitive); an -u ending would have marked it as the subject.
24.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembering, calling to mind, mentioning

25.meaning: He has prepared / made ready — to set something up in advance, to ready or get it in order beforehand.
25.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he prepared'). It belongs to the 'form IV' pattern (the a- prefix gives the sense of actively making something ready). With no added subject suffix, the bare form means 'he' did the action, completed in the past. The doubled middle letter (shadda) is part of this root.
25.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — to count, prepare, make ready

26.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
26.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

27.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
27.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

28.meaning: Forgiveness, pardon — the act of covering over and wiping away sins. Built on a sense of 'covering/shielding', it conveys both the concealing of faults and the remission of their consequences.
28.grammar: A verbal noun (the abstract notion of 'forgiving'). The ending -atan combines the feminine ending with the indefinite accusative marker (tanwīn). The accusative typically marks the noun as a direct object (the thing given or done), and the doubled-n sound ('nunation') signals that it is indefinite ('a/some forgiveness').

29.meaning: And a reward — in addition to the forgiveness and pleasure of Allah, the believers are promised a great reward (ʾajr ʿaẓīm — magnificent reward) for their faith and deeds.
29.grammar: Conjunction wāw + indefinite masculine noun ajr in the accusative case (manṣūb), marked by tanwīn fatḥ (-an).
29.root: أ-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — to reward; ajr = reward, recompense, wages

30.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
30.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: For / against a believer — one who has faith, who trusts and affirms; preceded by the preposition 'for/against.' The final -in (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a believer').
3.grammar: An active participle of Form IV (āmana, 'to believe'), meaning 'one who believes/has faith.' It is preceded by the preposition li- ('for/to'). The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation: genitive is the case taken after a preposition, and the nunation marks the noun as indefinite ('a believer').
3.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

4.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
4.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

5.meaning: "A believing woman" — a woman who has faith: one who accepts as true, trusts, and gives her heart's security to Allah. The underlying root joins the ideas of safety and trust, so a believer is one who entrusts herself and is thereby made secure.
5.grammar: An active participle of the causative (Form IV) pattern — the mu- prefix means "one who does" — made feminine by the -at ending, so "a believing woman." The final -in is a doubled kasra (nunation): the -n shows the word is indefinite ("a", not "the"), and the -i vowel is the genitive, the case used after a preposition or when the word hangs off a preceding noun in an "…of…" relation.

6.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
6.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: "He decided, decreed, settled, brought to completion" — to bring a matter to its conclusion by an authoritative determination: judging it, ordaining it, and thereby finishing it. The word combines deciding, decreeing and completing in one act.

parts.en: the root's final weak letter, written as alif

7.grammar: A completed-action verb (past tense) with no attached subject pronoun, which by default means "he" — one male (or a masculine subject) already did it. The verb comes from a root whose last letter is weak, so instead of a plain consonant the word ends in the long -ā vowel; the past tense also carries the sense of something settled and accomplished, not in progress.
7.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — deciding, decreeing, bringing to completion

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: "And His Messenger," the one sent with a message; "rasūl" denotes an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver something, here belonging to "Him."
9.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The base "rasūl" is a noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning "one who is sent." The suffix "-hu" is the attached possessive pronoun "his," placing the noun in a possessive "messenger of Him" relationship; the pronoun occupies the genitive slot.
9.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message or the one sent with it

10.meaning: A matter, affair, command, or thing to be done. It can mean an order issued or, more broadly, any business, situation, or decreed affair.
10.grammar: A noun in the accusative case with tanwīn (the -an ending), which marks it as indefinite and typically as the object of a verb ('a matter') or otherwise grammatically governed. The accusative shows it is being acted upon rather than acting.

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
11.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
11.root: — (particle; no root)

12.meaning: He/it is / he comes to be. A form of the verb kāna ('to be'), linking a subject to a state or asserting that something exists or occurs.
12.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 3rd person masculine; the final -a marks the subjunctive mood, the form a verb takes after particles meaning 'so that', 'in order to', or 'that'. It expresses a state being brought about rather than a plain fact.
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

13.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
13.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

14.meaning: the choice / the decision. Al-khiyara refers to the power or right of choice — the prerogative of selection. Here it emphasises that choosing belongs to Allah alone.

parts.en: the choice, the decision, the option (nominative)

14.grammar: Feminine noun in the nominative case (marfūʿ), -u (ḍamma) ending. Functions as the subject of a negated clause ('is not theirs').
14.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, preference; khiyara/khiyār: choice, option

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

16.meaning: A compound: 'their affair' / 'their matter' / 'their command' — the word 'amr' (a matter, affair, command, or situation) joined to the pronoun 'their.'
16.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, which appears when the word follows a preposition or is possessed/linked to another word ('… of …'). The suffix '-him' is 'their' (masculine plural); its vowel is 'i' (not '-hum') precisely because it follows the genitive '-i.'

17.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
17.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

18.meaning: 'Disobeys' / 'rebels against' — to defy a command and refuse to comply, the opposite of obeying.

parts.en: vowel on the medial letter (weak final letter dropped)

18.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he disobeys'), in the jussive/conditional mood. The root ends in a weak letter (ي); in the jussive that final ي is dropped entirely as the mood marker, leaving the medial letter ص carrying its kasra (-i) at the word's end. The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject; the shadda on the yā' is an assimilation (idghām) carried over in recitation from a preceding word.

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

20.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
20.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

21.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
21.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

22.meaning: He strayed, lost the way, or went off course — to wander from the right path, whether literally or figuratively (to err, be misguided, or deviate from truth and guidance).
22.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he went astray'. The bare past-tense form with the -a ending signals a single male (or thing) as the doer of a completed action.
22.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

23.meaning: straying / error — the state of being lost from the right path, wandering far from guidance and truth. A verbal noun naming the condition of going astray.
23.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) on the faʿāl pattern, naming the act/state of straying. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative — often used for the object of a verb or as an absolute object reinforcing a verb ('to stray a [great] straying') — and the -n shows it is indefinite.
23.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, get lost, err

24.meaning: An adjective meaning 'clear, plain, manifest' — describing something that is obvious and self-evident, or that makes things clear.
24.grammar: An active participle of form IV (mubīn), 'one that is manifest / makes clear.' The mu- prefix forms the participle. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative ending ('a clear one'), used here to agree with a preceding masculine accusative noun it describes.

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: You say / you were saying — a present-tense verb of speaking addressed to a single person. It expresses ongoing or habitual utterance.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person 'you' (masculine singular) subject, and the final '-u' is the indicative form, used for a plain ongoing statement ('you say'). The long 'ū' is the hollow root's middle letter surfacing.

3.meaning: 'to / for the One who…' — a preposition fused with a relative pronoun, introducing a clause that identifies someone by what they do ('the one who…').
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') joined to the masculine singular relative pronoun 'alladhī ('the one who/which'). A relative pronoun links to a following clause that describes its referent. Being a fixed particle, it does not change its ending for case.
3.root: — (relative pronoun; no root)

4.meaning: 'He bestowed favor / blessed / granted bounty' — a completed act of conferring grace, blessing, and comforts upon someone.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb on the 'afʿala' pattern, with a built-in sense of conferring something upon another. Its form marks a single masculine 'he' as the doer, with no attached subject suffix. So: 'he bestowed favor'.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

6.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
6.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

7.meaning: "And you bestowed favour / showed kindness, granted a blessing" — to confer a good thing generously upon someone, making their life pleasant and easy. The root carries the ideas of softness, ease and delightful blessing.
7.grammar: A completed-action (past tense) verb of the causative Form IV pattern (the a- prefix built into the stem turns "to be pleasant" into "to bestow something pleasant"). The suffix -ta is the doer: it marks a second-person singular masculine subject, "you (one man) did." Being past tense, the favour is presented as already conferred.
7.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — softness, ease, blessing and favour

8.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
8.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

9.meaning: Withhold, retain — amsik is a command to hold back, to keep, or to retain something and not let it go.
9.grammar: Form IV imperative verb (pattern afʿil), 2nd person masculine singular. Form IV imperatives regularly take hamzat al-waṣl at the beginning — this is standard morphology for Form IV imperatives, not an anomaly. The -ik with final sukūn is the regular Form IV imperative ending. The command is addressed to a single masculine recipient and means to retain or hold something back rather than releasing it.
9.root: م-س-ك (m-s-k) — to hold, to grasp, to retain, to withhold

10.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
10.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

11.meaning: "Your spouse" — one member of a pair that belongs together; used for a husband or a wife, and more broadly for a mate or counterpart that completes a couple.

parts.en: spouse, mate, one of a pair

11.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the form a noun takes when it is the object of a verb or governed by certain particles. The attached -ka means "your," addressed to a single male; because a possessor is attached, the noun is already definite and takes no -n (nunation).
11.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — pairing, coupling, joining two together

12.meaning: "And be mindful of / guard yourself against" — the command form of taqwā: to shield yourself by keeping a protective awareness of Allah, avoiding whatever earns His displeasure. It is not mere fright but a careful, self-protective consciousness of Allah.

parts.en: shield yourself, be wary, keep guard
command ending (the root's final weak letter dropped)

12.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one male. It belongs to the self-directed Form VIII pattern ("make a shield for yourself"), which is why the initial ا and the doubled t appear. The root's last letter is weak, and in commands that final weak letter falls away; the bare -i vowel left at the end is the trace of it, and it signals a singular masculine order — not a genitive case, since this is a verb.
12.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — shielding, guarding, protecting

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
13.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

14.meaning: "And you hide / keep concealed" — to cause something to remain unseen or unspoken, keeping it hidden inside rather than bringing it out.

parts.en: you (one person) — the u vowel marks the causative Form IV
final long vowel: plain statement (indicative) form

14.grammar: An ongoing-action verb (present/imperfect) of the causative Form IV pattern: the prefix tu- marks a second-person singular subject, "you," and its u vowel (rather than ta-) signals the causative "to make hidden." The root ends in a weak letter, so the verb closes in the long vowel -ī; that intact final -ī is the indicative form, used for straightforward statements of what is or keeps happening, as opposed to the shortened forms used after negation or command particles.

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: 'Yourself / your own self / your soul' — the noun 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner being) carrying the possessive 'your' (single male).
16.grammar: The noun 'nafs' ('self/soul') with the second-person masculine-singular possessive ending '-ka' (here '-ika'): 'your self'. The attached possessive can sit on any case, so it alone does not mark subject or object.
16.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being of a person

17.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
17.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

19.meaning: "The one who brings it out into the open / makes it appear" — the discloser of it: whoever causes something hidden to become visible and known.
19.grammar: An active participle ("one who does") of the causative Form IV pattern: mu- means "the one who," and the base sense "to appear" becomes "to make appear." Because the root ends in a weak letter, the participle closes in -ī, and a participle like this can govern an object the way a verb does — hence the attached pronoun -hi ("it/him"). The i vowel of -hi is the regular shape this pronoun takes after an -ī.

20.meaning: "And you fear / stand in awe" — a reverent dread that comes from recognising the greatness of the one feared, mixed with knowledge and reverence rather than mere panic. It also covers the wary fear of an unwanted outcome.

parts.en: the root's final weak letter, written as alif

20.grammar: An ongoing-action verb (present/imperfect). The prefix ta- marks the subject as second-person singular, "you." The root's last letter is weak, so the verb ends in the long -ā vowel; verbs ending this way do not show the mood vowel outwardly, so this is the ordinary statement (indicative) form, describing what one does or keeps doing.

21.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
21.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
21.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

22.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
22.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
22.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

23.meaning: An adjective meaning 'more entitled, having a better/greater right, more deserving' of something.
23.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the afʿal pattern, meaning 'more/most entitled'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word serves as the subject or as a predicate describing the subject.
23.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, just claim, what is due

24.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
24.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

25.meaning: "You fear Him / hold Him in awe" — to feel reverent dread of Him, the awe that grows out of knowing His greatness rather than blind fright.

parts.en: fear with awe (root's final weak letter written as alif)

25.grammar: An ongoing-action verb (present/imperfect) with an attached object pronoun. The prefix ta- marks a second-person singular subject, "you"; the long -ā at the end of the stem is the weak final root letter, and such verbs show no visible mood vowel, so this is the plain statement (indicative) form. The suffix -hu is the object, "him/it" — the one feared, not the one fearing.

26.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
26.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

27.meaning: He decreed, ordained, settled, or brought to a definitive conclusion — to decide a matter and carry it through so that it is fixed and accomplished. It carries the sense of an authoritative, final determination.
27.grammar: A past-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject — 'he' did the action, completed and in the past. There is no separate suffix; the bare verb form itself signals 'he'. The final root letter appears as a long 'ā' (written with a dagger alif) because this verb's third root letter is a weak vowel.
27.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decree, conclude, settle, and accomplish

28.meaning: Zayd — a man's personal name. As a name its job is simply to identify an individual, though the form is built from a root meaning "increase, growth, addition," so it reads as "increase/abundance."
28.grammar: A proper name treated as a fully declinable noun. The ending -un is a doubled ḍamma (nunation): the -u vowel is the nominative, the case a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being described, and the -n is the sign that the word is not made definite by al-. Personal names commonly keep this nunation when their pattern allows it.

29.meaning: From it / from her — marking the starting point or source out of which something comes, referring to a feminine or grammatically-feminine thing.
29.grammar: The preposition 'from/out of' attached to the pronoun -hā ('it/her'), which refers back to a feminine or grammatically-feminine noun. After a preposition this pronoun stands in the genitive (object) position, giving the sense 'from it' — the source or point of departure of an action.

30.meaning: A need, want, or errand — something a person requires, desires, or has an interest in settling; the business or claim one has yet to see through.
30.grammar: A singular noun. The ending -an is a doubled fatḥa (nunation): the -a vowel marks the accusative, the case used when a noun is the object of a verb or otherwise governed as such, and the -n shows it is indefinite — "a need," not "the need."
30.root: و-ط-ر (w-ṭ-r) — a need or want one aims to fulfil

31.meaning: "We joined her in marriage to you" — to pair two people as spouses, giving one in marriage to the other; from the idea of making two things into a matched couple.
31.grammar: A completed-action (past tense) verb of the doubled-middle-letter Form II pattern, which makes a plain sense transitive/causative: from "being a pair" to "making into a pair." The suffix -nā is the doer, first-person plural "we." Two object pronouns then follow in order — -ka "you" and -hā "her" — a verb of this kind being able to take two objects (giving someone to someone). The past tense presents the act as already accomplished.

32.meaning: A two-word particle phrase meaning "so that, in order that" — it introduces a purpose or intended result.
32.grammar: A compound purpose particle. It introduces a goal and causes the following present-tense verb to take the subjunctive mood (a verb ending in -a), expressing "in order that he may …". It does not change for person or number.

33.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
33.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

34.meaning: He/it is / he comes to be. A form of the verb kāna ('to be'), linking a subject to a state or asserting that something exists or occurs.
34.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 3rd person masculine; the final -a marks the subjunctive mood, the form a verb takes after particles meaning 'so that', 'in order to', or 'that'. It expresses a state being brought about rather than a plain fact.
34.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

35.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
35.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
35.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

36.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
36.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

37.meaning: Tightness, constriction, or distress of the heart — a sense of being hemmed in, hence unease, difficulty, or the kind of moral discomfort felt when something weighs on one. By extension it can mean blame or sin that constricts the conscience.
37.grammar: The -un ending (nunation) marks an indefinite noun ('a ___ / any ___') in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described as existing.

38.meaning: The preposition 'in / within / during.' It places something inside a container, period, place, or matter.
38.grammar: A preposition. It governs the noun that follows, putting it in the genitive case and situating something inside it — in space, in time ('during'), or in a circumstance.

39.meaning: "Spouses, wives" — the plural of zawj: the partners who together make up couples, each one the mate and counterpart of the other.
39.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun. The -i ending is the genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition or when it hangs off a preceding noun; the absence of the indefinite -n (nunation) shows it is the first term of a possessive chain — "the spouses OF …" — so it is waiting on a following word to complete the sense.
39.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — pairing, coupling, joining two together

40.meaning: "Their claimed/adopted sons" — plural of daʿī, one who is *called* somebody's son: a boy attributed to a man by the naming of adoption rather than by birth.
40.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive ending, used after a preposition or when the noun is possessed by or linked to something else. The attached -him means "their," referring to a masculine plural group, and its i vowel is the regular shape this pronoun takes after an -i ending; the possessor also makes the noun definite, so no -n (nunation) appears.

41.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
41.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

42.meaning: "They finished, settled, brought to an end" — to carry a matter through to its completion or to discharge what was due, so that nothing of it remains outstanding.

parts.en: they (a group of males) did it

42.grammar: A completed-action (past tense) verb whose ending -aw marks a third-person masculine plural subject: "they (men) did." Normally this plural subject ending is -ū, but because the root's final letter is weak that letter drops out and the ending appears as -aw (the silent alif after the wāw is only spelling). The past tense presents the matter as already concluded.

43.meaning: A small phrase meaning 'from them' or 'of them,' referring to a group of females. It combines the preposition min (from, of, some of) with an attached 'them' (feminine).
43.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. Min means 'from,' 'out of,' or 'some of.' The pronoun -hunna means 'them' for a group of females; after the n of min it keeps its base vowel -u (hunna). The combination commonly expresses source, origin, or a part taken from a whole.

44.meaning: A need, want, or errand — something a person requires, desires, or has an interest in settling; the business or claim one has yet to see through.
44.grammar: A singular noun. The ending -an is a doubled fatḥa (nunation): the -a vowel marks the accusative, the case used when a noun is the object of a verb or otherwise governed as such, and the -n shows it is indefinite — "a need," not "the need."
44.root: و-ط-ر (w-ṭ-r) — a need or want one aims to fulfil

45.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
45.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

46.meaning: 'Command, order, affair, matter.' This noun covers both a directive that is commanded and a situation or affair that comes to pass — what is decreed or what is the case.
46.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.

47.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
47.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

48.meaning: Done, carried out, accomplished — a thing brought into effect. A passive participle naming something that has been or is to be acted upon and fulfilled, hence 'a deed accomplished' or 'a matter destined to be'.
48.grammar: A passive participle of the 'mafʿūl' pattern, naming the thing that an action is done to ('that which is done/carried out'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, which commonly marks the word as an object or as a descriptive complement ('as a thing accomplished').

1.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
1.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
3.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
3.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

4.meaning: The Prophet — a person who receives revelation from Allah and announces it, one given prophetic news and inspired tidings from the unseen.
4.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'the'. The final -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive chain, follows a preposition, or marks agreement with a preceding genitive word. The article's l assimilates into the following n (an-nabiy), since n is a 'sun letter'.
4.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; to inform, announce

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'constriction, hardship, blame, or discomfort' — a sense of being hemmed in, whether physical difficulty or moral fault.
6.grammar: A singular noun. The ending -in (genitive with nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a difficulty / any blame') and is the case typically used after a preposition.
6.root: ح-ر-ج (ḥ-r-j) — narrowness, constriction, difficulty

7.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
7.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb whose core sense is 'to make obligatory, impose as a duty, ordain'; it also carries the related senses 'to appoint/allot a fixed share' and 'to undertake / bind oneself to a duty'. As shown, it means 'he made obligatory / he ordained'.
8.grammar: A completed (past) action in the basic faʿala pattern for a third-person masculine singular doer ('he/one [did it]'). There is no separable subject suffix on this form: the final fatḥa (-a) sitting on the last root letter is part of the verb stem itself, not an added ending, and the doer 'he' is understood from the pattern alone. A separate pronoun-suffix would appear only for other subjects (for example -tu 'I', -ta/-ti 'you', -tum 'you all').
8.root: ف-ر-ض (f-r-ḍ) — making obligatory; ordaining a fixed duty or share

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
9.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

10.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
10.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

11.meaning: An established way, practice, or norm; a consistent pattern of conduct that is followed as a precedent. When ascribed to Allah it denotes His unchanging way of dealing with creation.
11.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, marked by the final -a (often an object, or set as an emphatic statement). As the first term of a possessive pairing it links to a following noun, meaning 'the way of …'.
11.root: س-ن-ن (s-n-n) — to set a precedent; an established way

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
14.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

15.meaning: They were alone, withdrew in private, or were by themselves apart from others; to be in seclusion or privacy with someone.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb from a weak root, so the plural ending appears as -aw (written with a silent final alif). It means 'they' for a group of males and marks a completed action: 'they were alone / withdrew in private.'
15.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty, alone, secluded; privacy

16.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
16.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

17.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
17.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
17.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

18.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
18.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

19.meaning: 'Command, order, affair, matter.' This noun covers both a directive that is commanded and a situation or affair that comes to pass — what is decreed or what is the case.
19.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.

20.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
20.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

21.meaning: A measure that has been determined — a decree, an apportioned amount, the exact measure allotted to something. The root joins the ideas of measuring out, having power to determine, and fixing a due proportion, so the word covers both "decree" and "precise measure."
21.grammar: A singular noun. The ending -an is a doubled fatḥa (nunation): the -a vowel is the accusative, the case a noun takes as the object of a verb or in similar governed positions, and the -n marks it as indefinite — "a decree," not "the decree."
21.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — measuring out, determining, power to apportion

22.meaning: "Measured out, determined, decreed" — describing something that has been precisely apportioned and fixed by a deciding power, so that it comes about exactly as measured.

parts.en: passive-participle prefix: "having been …"; the doubling mark on it is a recitation sign, showing that a preceding n-sound merges into this m

22.grammar: A passive participle on the mafʿūl pattern — the ma- prefix plus the long -ū inside makes it "a thing that has been done to," i.e. measured and decreed rather than measuring. The doubling (shadda) written over the initial m is not part of the word's own structure: it records assimilation in recitation, an immediately preceding n-sound (a nūn or nunation) being absorbed into this m. The ending -an is a doubled fatḥa: the -a is the accusative, the case used for objects and for words governed as such, and the -n shows the word is indefinite.

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: "They convey / deliver, make (a message) reach its destination" — to pass something on until it arrives complete in the hands of those meant to receive it. The root is about reaching a goal, so conveying here means bringing a message all the way to its target.

parts.en: he/they (third person) — the u vowel marks the transitive Form II
they (a group of males); the final -na marks the plain statement form

2.grammar: An ongoing-action verb (present/imperfect) of the doubled-middle-letter Form II pattern, which turns "to reach" into "to make reach." The prefix yu- marks a third-person subject and its u vowel signals that Form II shape; the suffix -ūna is the subject, third-person masculine plural "they." Keeping the final -na is the mark of the indicative — a straightforward statement of what they do — since that -na drops away when the verb follows particles that subjunctivise or negate it.
2.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — reaching, arriving, attaining a goal

3.meaning: Messages — the communications or dispatches entrusted to be delivered; the plural of a single 'message'.
3.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks 'more than two' of a feminine word). The final -i is the ending that sound feminine plurals take in both the genitive ('of …' / after a preposition) and the object (accusative) roles — for this class of plural the two share one form.
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching, messengership

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: "And they fear Him / hold Him in awe" — reverent dread arising from recognition of His majesty, a fear coupled with knowledge and reverence rather than mere alarm.

parts.en: they (a group of males); the -na marks the plain statement form

5.grammar: An ongoing-action verb (present/imperfect) with an attached object pronoun. The prefix ya- marks a third-person masculine subject and the suffix marks it as plural, "they" — normally -ūna, but because the root's last letter is weak it appears as -awna. Retaining the final -na is the sign of the indicative, the ordinary statement form used for what people do or keep doing. The closing -hu is the object, "Him" — the one feared.

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: 'They fear' or 'they hold in awe' — experiencing khashya, a fear mixed with reverence and awareness of someone's greatness, especially the kind of dread that comes from knowledge of the one feared.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The -awna ending marks a masculine-plural 'they' subject (the long final root-vowel blends into the plural ending) and the indicative mood, which states the action as an ongoing or habitual fact.
7.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — fear blended with awe and reverence

8.meaning: Anyone / a single one: 'one' used to mean a sole individual, especially in negative or conditional contexts ('not anyone', 'any single person').
8.grammar: A noun meaning 'one / a single one', frequently used for 'anyone' when paired with a negation. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for a verb's object.

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

11.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
11.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
11.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

12.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
12.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
12.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

13.meaning: 'A reckoner / one who takes full account' — one who reckons, calculates, and holds to account, weighing every deed and giving each its exact due. It also carries the sense of being entirely sufficient as such an accountant.
13.grammar: A singular masculine noun/adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern (a thorough, capable reckoner). The ending -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, here marking the word as a specifying or circumstantial complement — telling in what capacity something is regarded ('as a reckoner'). The final nunation signals indefiniteness ('a…').
13.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to count, calculate, reckon, hold to account

1.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
1.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: Muḥammad — a masculine proper name meaning 'the praised one' or 'one worthy of much praise', built on the pattern of intensive/repeated praise.
3.grammar: A proper name of the passive-participle 'mufaʿʿal' (intensive) pattern, meaning 'highly praised'. The final -un (nunation) marks it as nominative — the case used for a subject or for the thing being identified/named.
3.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — praise, commendation

4.meaning: "Father" — a male parent, and by extension a forefather, ancestor, or one who stands in a father's place of care and authority.

parts.en: object (accusative) ending, shown as a long vowel

4.grammar: A noun belonging to a small special group ("father," "brother," "father-in-law," and the like) that shows its case with a long vowel instead of a short one when it is linked to a following possessor. The long -ā is the accusative form, used when the noun is the object of a verb or governed as such; the same word would appear as -ū when it is the subject and -ī after a preposition or in an "…of…" link.

5.meaning: One; anyone; a single individual. Often used in negative or conditional contexts to mean 'anyone (at all)'.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The -in ending combines the genitive marker -i (the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link, '… of …') with nunation (-n), the sign of an indefinite 'a / any'.

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

7.meaning: The plural noun 'men' joined to a 'your (plural)' pronoun — 'your men', i.e. the adult males of your community or group.
7.grammar: A plural noun (singular rajul, 'man') with the attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your', for a group). The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or when one noun is possessed by another ('… of …'); -kum makes it 'your men'.
7.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manhood, going on foot

8.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
8.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

9.meaning: A messenger, envoy — one who is sent with a message on behalf of the sender; in scripture, a prophet commissioned to deliver Allah's message to people.

parts.en: messenger, one sent with a message; the doubling mark on the r is a recitation sign, showing that a preceding n-sound merges into it

9.grammar: A singular noun of the intensive/steady pattern faʿūl, describing the one who carries out the sending-errand. The doubling (shadda) written over the initial r belongs to recitation, not to the word's own structure: it records an immediately preceding n-sound (a nūn or nunation) being absorbed into this r. The -a ending is the accusative, the case a noun takes as the object of a verb or when governed by particles that require it; the absence of the indefinite -n (nunation) shows the word is bound to a following noun in an "…of…" relation, so it awaits the naming of the one who sent him.
9.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching with a message

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: A seal or signet — the stamp pressed onto a document to close and authenticate it. By extension it names the one who seals a series: the final member after whom nothing further is added, the closure and confirmation of what came before.

parts.en: seal, signet; the one who seals/concludes

11.grammar: A noun with the connector wa ("and") in front. The final -a is the accusative ending: it typically marks a noun as the object of a verb, or as a word being asserted/predicated about something. Because the noun carries no -n (tanwīn), it is in a possessive link with a following noun — literally "seal OF …".
11.root: خ-ت-م (kh-t-m) — sealing, stamping shut, bringing to a close

12.meaning: 'The prophets' — those whom Allah selects to receive revelation and convey His message. The plural of nabī, a prophet who brings news from Allah.
12.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the genitive-or-accusative case — the form used when the noun is a direct object or governed by a preposition, as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject.
12.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; hence a prophet who brings news from Allah

13.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

15.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
15.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

16.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
16.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
16.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

17.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
17.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
3.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

4.meaning: 'Remember! / call to mind, mention' — a command to bring something to mind, keep it in memory, or speak of it.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you.' The '-ū' ending directs the order to a group ('you all remember!'); the initial connecting 'a-' is a helping vowel that lets the word begin.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: Remembrance, mention, recollection, or invocation; the act of calling something to mind or naming it — often the mindful mention and invocation of Allah.
6.grammar: A verbal noun (the act of remembering/mentioning). The final -an (accusative case with nunation) commonly marks it as a direct object or as a specifying word ('… in respect of remembrance'), and the nunation makes it indefinite. So it reads 'a remembrance / (in) remembrance'.
6.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind, invoke

7.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
7.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (the 'tanwīn' of fatḥa). The accusative case here commonly marks an object of a verb or an indefinite quantity; the doubled-n sound (nunation) signals that the word is indefinite ('many', not 'the many').
7.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

1.meaning: A command addressed to a group: declare Him utterly free of every fault, flaw and unworthy description — the act called tasbīḥ, praising by removing all imperfection from Him rather than merely complimenting Him.

parts.en: declare (Him) free of all imperfection, glorify

1.grammar: An imperative (command) verb of the doubled/intensive pattern (Form II), which turns the root sense into "to pronounce something to be pure/free of fault". The -ū ending means the command is given to a group of males (or a mixed group), not one person. The final -hu is an attached object pronoun, "him".
1.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to glide or swim swiftly onward; in Form II, to declare Allah free of all imperfection

2.meaning: Morning, daybreak, the early part of the day — the time from dawn until mid-morning.

parts.en: accusative ending on feminine noun (with nunation)

2.grammar: A feminine noun (its feminine ending is the tied-tā', pronounced '-t-' before the case vowel). The '-an' accusative ending here typically marks a time expression ('in the morning'), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.
2.root: ب-ك-ر (b-k-r) — early morning, to be early

3.meaning: And in the evening — the late afternoon / evening time. Together with bukratan (in the morning), it forms a merism indicating glorifying Allah at all times, specifically at dawn and dusk.

parts.en: in the evening / at eventide (indefinite accusative of time)

3.grammar: Indefinite masculine noun in the accusative case as an adverb of time (ẓarf al-zamān). Tanwīn fatḥ (-an) marks indefinite accusative.
3.root: أ-ص-ل (ʾ-ṣ-l) — origin, root; aṣīl = late afternoon / evening (the time when things return to their origin)

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'he prays' or 'he performs the ritual prayer' — to worship through the formal prayer, and more broadly to invoke blessing.
3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he prays / is praying'). The yu- prefix marks an ongoing or future action by 'he'; the weak final root letter appears as the long -ī ending. The doubled middle letter belongs to a form conveying earnest, deliberate action.
3.root: ص-ل-و / ص-ل-ي (ṣ-l-w/y) — prayer, worship, invoking blessing

4.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
4.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

5.meaning: The angels — created beings of light who carry out Allah's commands and convey His messages; the plural of malak, "messenger/emissary".
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with wa ("and") prefixed. The -u ending is nominative: it generally marks a word as the subject or doer of a sentence, or as the thing being spoken about. The attached -hu means "his", and because a possessor pronoun is attached the noun takes no -n (tanwīn).
5.root: ء-ل-ك (ʾ-l-k) — to bear or deliver a message

6.meaning: A purpose clause: "so that He may bring you out / lead you forth" — expressing the aim or intended result of an action, namely one party causing a group to come out of something.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb of the causative pattern (Form IV): the plain root means "to go out", and this pattern makes it "to make/bring out". The yu- prefix means the doer is a single third person, "he". The li- in front means "so that" and pulls the verb into the subjunctive, which is why the ending is a plain -a instead of -u: it signals intention or purpose rather than a bare statement of fact. The final -kum is the object pronoun "you (plural)".
6.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — going out, emerging, exiting

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: Darknesses, layers of gloom; the manifold states of being deprived of light, whether literal or as a figure for ignorance and error.
8.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ("the darknesses"). The -i ending here is genitive — the case taken by this plural after a preposition (the -āt plural shows genitive with -i rather than the -a it would take in the accusative). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").
8.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; also wrongdoing and injustice

9.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
9.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

10.meaning: Light — radiance and illumination that dispels darkness; often a figure for guidance, truth, and clarity.
10.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ("… OF …"). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").

11.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence

12.meaning: Refers to 'the believers' — those who have faith, who trust and affirm Allah and what He has revealed. The whole word is prefixed with 'with/in/by', so it carries the sense 'with/in the believers'.
12.grammar: An active participle in the plural, made definite by 'al-' (the) and governed by the preposition 'bi' (with/in/by). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the non-subject (accusative/genitive) state; after a preposition like 'bi' it functions as a genitive ('with/in the believers'). The 'mu-' prefix marks it as a doer — 'one who brings about faith,' i.e. a believer.
12.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to have faith

13.meaning: 'Most Merciful, ever-compassionate' — one who continually and abundantly shows mercy. On the faʿīl pattern it conveys a deep, settled, characteristic quality of mercy.
13.grammar: An adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern denoting a permanent trait. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a most merciful …'), commonly marking the object/complement of a verb or an adjective agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun.

1.meaning: Their greeting / salutation — the words of well-wishing and peace exchanged in welcome; here belonging to a group.
1.grammar: A noun (a Form II verbal noun meaning 'a greeting/wishing-of-life') ending in the nominative -u, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence. The attached -hum means 'their'. So: 'their greeting'.
1.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — to live; to greet with a wish of life

2.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
2.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
2.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

3.meaning: They meet / encounter it (or Him): a plural action of coming face to face with something or someone, often used of arriving at and confronting an appointed reckoning.
3.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, 3rd person masculine plural, from a weak-final (defective) root whose last letter is a yāʾ. In the singular this verb is yalqā; in the masculine plural the weak final letter drops and the plural ending -ūna fuses with the stem vowel to surface as the diphthong -awna (hence yalqawna, 'they meet'). The ya- prefix plus this plural ending mean 'they (masculine) do' an ongoing or yet-to-happen act. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it'.
3.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come upon

4.meaning: Peace, soundness, safety, well-being — freedom from harm and discord; a word of greeting and of the wholeness and security that comes from being safe and at peace.
